# Visitor information

[Home](https://www.catharijneconvent.nl/)  »  Visitor information

Welcome to Museum Catharijneconvent!

A visit to medieval Utrecht is not complete without a visit to Museum Catharijneconvent. Wander the halls of a medieval monastery and be enchanted by the most beautiful collection of medieval art in the Netherlands.

Marvel at the glittering gold and silver in the Treasury, admire paintings by Rembrandt, Jan Steen and their contemporaries and visit our unique temporary exhibitions.

## Exhibition Finding Meaning

March 21st - August 30th 

What do a doctor, an MMA champion, and a drag queen have in common? More than you might think. They all ask themselves the same fundamental question: what truly gives life meaning? Eight people with very different backgrounds took on the challenge and curated this deeply personal exhibition.

For centuries, people have searched for meaning through religion and spirituality, personal growth, social connections or things that bring a sense of wonder or excitement. Some find meaning by focusing on others, others by focusing on themselves. Meaning can come from something lasting or something that offers immediate results. But are any of these more meaningful than the others?

An ultimate form of meaning doesn't exist, but a sense of meaning is essential for a happy life. And often it takes a major event or period in your life to make you question where you find yours.

Meet eight people from very different backgrounds who share their personal stories about finding meaning. What drives them, and how do they live their lives? They tell their stories through objects they have chosen from the museum's collection, giving these artworks new significance. At the same time they invite you to reflect on how you give your own life meaning.

## Catharijneconvent - A building with a history

Museum Catharijneconvent occupies a characteristic building in the old city centre of Utrecht. The building has a long history going back to the fourteenth century. Originally, it was the site of a shelter for the homeless. In the fifteenth century the Carmelites acquired the land and built a convent. Later, the knights of St John turned it into a hospital, which it remained until the beginning of the nineteenth century. Subsequently it served various other functions until becoming a museum in 1979.

## Opening hours & admission

**Opening hours**

- Tuesday - Friday 10am - 5pm
- Saturday, Sunday and holidays 11am - 5pm
- Closed on Mondays, 1 January and 27 April

### **Admission**

- ICOM, AICA, Museumkaart: Free\*
- Children under 17: Free
- Students: €8,00 | Online €7,00
- 65+\*: €14.50\* | Online €13,50
- Adults\*: €16,00 | Online €15,00

\*A surcharge may apply to temporary exhibitions.

Our temporary exhibitions are fully accessible for English-speaking visitors. For the permanent collection, a free audio guide is available in English.

**Please note that our two 'Utrecht galleries' are temporarily closed at the moment.**

**Pin-only** 
Paying in cash is no longer possible at our museum.

[Order your tickets online](https://tickets.catharijneconvent.nl/Exhibitions/Register?ID=16393a13-71d0-ec11-a2e5-de402710edd8)

## Groups, tour operators & facilities

### **Groups & tour operators**

Various options are available for a visit with a group or tour operator.

We will be happy to tell you more. You can find [more information on this page](https://www.catharijneconvent.nl/group-visits-tours/) and/or contact our Group visits department at: [groepsbezoek@catharijneconvent.nl](mailto:groepsbezoek@catharijneconvent.nl).

### 

### **Facilities**

There is a museum shop, museum café and outdoor seating area, meeting rooms and a library on site.

## Welcome to the Frans Hals Museum

The Frans Hals Museum is Haarlem’s museum of fine arts. It houses the largest collection of Frans Hals paintings in the world, as well as works by other famous artists from Haarlem such as Judith Leyster, Cornelis van Haarlem and Jacob van Ruisdael. You’ll also discover an extensive collection of art from 1880 to the present day, including works by Isaac Israëls, Charley Toorop and Dana Lixenberg.

Discover 16th- and 17th-century, modern and contemporary art in the old city centre of Haarlem.

## News

[News overviewNews overview](https://kunsthal.nl/en/news/)

### Brenda Poels new Chair of the Supervisory Board

Starting 1 December 2026

Date

2 November 2026

Brenda Poels has been appointed Chair of the Supervisory Board of Kunsthal Rotterdam, starting her duties on 1 December 2026.

[Brenda Poels new Chair of the Supervisory Board](https://kunsthal.nl/en/news/brenda-poels-new-chair-of-the-supervisory-board/)

### Kunsthal Rotterdam wins the Museumtijdschrift Exhibition Award 2026

Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses

Date

7 October 2026

The exhibition Iris van Herpen: Sculpting the Senses was announced as the winner of the 2026 Museumtijdschrift Exhibition Prize on 7 October.

[Kunsthal Rotterdam wins the Museumtijdschrift Exhibition Award 2026](https://kunsthal.nl/en/news/kunsthal-rotterdam-wins-the-museumtijdschrift-exhibition-award-2026/)

### Exhibitions to look forward to

Kunsthal Highlights 2027

Date

5 October 2026

In 2027, Kunsthal Rotterdam will once again present a diverse and richly contrasting programme in its main galleries, featuring a wide range of artists, creators and stories – from Monira Al Qadiri and Jean Jullien to Luigi & Iango. The year will draw to a grand close in December with an impressive exhibition by Anish Kapoor.

[Exhibitions to look forward to](https://kunsthal.nl/en/news/exhibitions-to-look-forward-to/)

### Exhibition of work by cartoonist Jip van den Toorn

On display from 7 November

Date

1 October 2026

Experience the world through the eyes of Jip van den Toorn and discover how, with humor and a sharp eye, she captures our increasingly unpredictable world in her drawings.

[Exhibition of work by cartoonist Jip van den Toorn](https://kunsthal.nl/en/news/kunsthal-rotterdam-presents-an-exhibition-of-work-by-cartoonist-jip-van-den-toorn/)

### Kunsthal presents photo exhibition about 50 years North Sea Jazz

On display from 5 September

Date

26 August 2026

This year, North Sea Jazz is celebrating its 50th anniversary. On the occasion of this landmark, Kunsthal Rotterdam presents 50 Years North Sea Jazz Photography.

[Kunsthal presents photo exhibition about 50 years North Sea Jazz](https://kunsthal.nl/en/news/kunsthal-presents-photo-exhibition-about-50-years-north-sea-jazz/)

### Photo exhibition about Europe’s largest greenhouse complex

Plastic Sea, Perfect Storm

Date

26 August 2026

This autumn, the photographer Rob Hornstra and the author Arnold van Bruggen will show how countless migrants have to produce food for European markets.

[Photo exhibition about Europe’s largest greenhouse complex](https://kunsthal.nl/en/news/photo-exhibition-reveals-distressing-world-behind-europes-largest-greenhouse-complex/)

### Kunsthal Rotterdam presents The Grand Summer Hut

On view until 30 August

Date

24 July 2026

This summer, visitors to the Kunsthal are invited to discover The Grand Summer Hut, a playful and colourful experience designed by Rotterdam-based graphic artist Teuntje Fleur.

[Kunsthal Rotterdam presents The Grand Summer Hut](https://kunsthal.nl/en/news/kunsthal-rotterdam-presents-the-grand-summer-hut/)

### Exhibition on Paul Signac in the Kunsthal

On display from 24 October

Date

15 July 2026

From Saturday 24 October 2026, Kunsthal Rotterdam will be dedicating a large-scale retrospective to Paul Signac (1863–1935).

[Exhibition on Paul Signac in the Kunsthal](https://kunsthal.nl/en/news/exhibition-on-paul-signac-in-the-kunsthal/)

## The Collection

Experience brilliantly coloured paintings from the West Coast

[> The real attraction for me was the gallery's collection of Nordic painters. Goteborgs konstmuseum has possibly the best collection of Nordic painters in the whole of Sweden. > > **Visitor** From Tripadvisor](https://www.tripadvisor.se/Attraction_Review-g189894-d232080-Reviews-Museum_of_Fine_Art_Goteborgs_Konstmuseum-Gothenburg_Vastra_Gotaland_County_West_Co.html)

Great work of mixing old and new pieces from the collection and giving the exhibition such an interesting twist! > > **Visitor on their Instagram** 18 Dec 2016](https://www.tripadvisor.se/Attraction_Review-g189894-d232080-Reviews-Museum_of_Fine_Art_Goteborgs_Konstmuseum-Gothenburg_Vastra_Gotaland_County_West_Co.html)

[> Visiting the Gothenburg Museum of Art was one of the highlights of my stay in the city. > > **Karen Bryan, Blogger** Europe a la carte, 8 Dec 2016](http://www.europealacarte.co.uk/blog/2016/12/08/art-museum-gothemburg/) [> I took a walk through Gothenburg and discovered the museum of art. At the end my visit took 2 hours longer than I planned to spend in the city, because I really enjoyed exploring all the artworks and the temporary exhibition in this nice building. As a student the entry was free! :-) > > **Visitor** From TripAdvidsor](https://www.tripadvisor.se/Attraction_Review-g189894-d232080-Reviews-Museum_of_Fine_Art_Goteborgs_Konstmuseum-Gothenburg_Vastra_Gotaland_County_West_Co.html)

> The museum houses art (mainly paintings) from the last 500 years or so. We were pleased to see such a wide-range of artists' work displayed - both those from Scandinavia but also those more well-known to us such as Picasso, Munch, Van Gogh, Kandinsky and Monet.
> 
> **Visitor** From TripAdvidsor

## Book a Private Guided Tour

Did you know that you can book private guided tours at the museum, for both personal occasions and events for companies and societies? A private guided tour can be a wonderful surprise for someone you wish to celebrate, or an inspirational experience for you and your coworkers. Perhaps you will become aware of new contexts and new ways to see art, or notice details that you did not know existed. The guided tours are led by our art educators, who adapt the content to your specific interests. Read more about the different themes below.

### Themes for Private Guided Tours

[**Highlights of the collection**\\ \\ Let our art educator present highlights of our collection, featuring the foremost artists and artworks. Or, if you prefer, the tour can be adapted to suit your personal highlights!\\ \\ Continued](https://goteborgskonstmuseum.se/en/book-a-tour-highlights-of-the-collection/) [**Life and death in art**\\ \\ Art depicts all the phases of life – including death. We take a closer look at how artists have depicted life and death in both historical and contemporary art.\\ \\ Continued](https://goteborgskonstmuseum.se/en/book-a-tour-life-and-death-in-art/) [**Art and mental illness**\\ \\ In what way can art create suffering, or suffering create art? What is the connection between creativity and the unconscious forces of the psyche?\\ \\ Continued](https://goteborgskonstmuseum.se/en/book-a-tour-art-and-mental-illness/) [**Nudity in art**\\ \\ Have you ever wondered why so many artworks show the nude body? On this tour we get under the skin of the nude artworks at the Gothenburg Museum of Art.\\ \\ Continued](https://goteborgskonstmuseum.se/en/book-a-tour-nudity-in-art/) [**What is art?**\\ \\ We investigate contemporary art in the collection, emphasizing its diversity of materials and expressions. What is art? What could be art? Who decides, and where are the boundaries, if there are any?\\ \\ Continued](https://goteborgskonstmuseum.se/en/book-a-tour-what-is-art/) [**Nordic fin-de-siècle and the Fürstenberg Gallery**\\ \\ Hear more about the unique collection of Nordic fin-de-siècle art in the Fürstenberg Gallery. We travel through time from 19th century history painting to the lyrical “Nordic light”.\\ \\ Continued](https://goteborgskonstmuseum.se/en/book-a-tour-nordic-fin-de-siecle-and-the-furstenberg-gallery/) [**Explore the Queer in Art**\\ \\ Norms are the unwritten rules that we all have to relate to on a daily basis. On this tour, we examine art from the perspective of gender studies and a critique of norms – something that can teach us a lot about both history and the present time.\\ \\ Continued](https://goteborgskonstmuseum.se/en/book-a-tour-norms-in-art/)

## Upcoming exhibition

[**Otobong Nkanga**\\ \\ I dreamt of you in colours 10.10 2026 – 28.3 2027\\ \\ In the autumn’s exhibition at Malmö Konsthall, visitors encounter the multidisciplinary artistic practice of Otobong Nkanga in the first large-scale presentation of her work in Sweden. Leaning on strategies of resistance, she poetically highlights the links between racialised capitalism and the accelerating climate crisis.](https://malmokonsthall.se/en/utstallningar/otobong-nkanga/)

### Visit us

Malmö Konsthall curates art that challenges and inspires. We present three to four exhibitions per year, with both local and international artists.

Enjoy one of the largest and most diverse selections of art books in the south of Sweden. In Malmö Konsthall’s bookshop you can find the perfect gift for a friend, or expand your own knowledge of the contemporary art scene.

# The Thiel Gallery

---

The Thiel Gallery is recognized as one of the finest art museums in Sweden and is beautifully set in walled grounds at Blockhusudden in the royal park of Djurgården. The gallery houses a unique collection of works of art from the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries by leading artists of the period including Eugène Jansson, Carl Larsson, Bruno Liljefors, Edvard Munch, August Strindberg and Anders Zorn. 

[Learn more](https://www.thielskagalleriet.se/en/museum/about-the-gallery/)

metadata.description: Bildmuseet is one of Sweden’s foremost venues for international contemporary art, a part of Umeå University and the public heart of its Arts campus. On seven floors of striking architecture, the fields of Art, Humanities and Science combine to consider key issues of our time. Bildmuseet is a place for stimulating encounters and conversations about art, society and existence. The exhibitions are produced in collaboration with artists, museums and universities worldwide, and often attract both national and international attention. As a visitor, you are invited to participate in guided tours and creative workshops, listen to artist talks, debates, lectures and live music, watch film screenings and attend other events, all with free admission. After 30 years of operation, Bildmuseet moved to the new museum building in 2012 on the banks of the Umeälven River, right next to Umeå Academy of Fine Arts, Umeå Institute of Design and Umeå School of Architecture. The new museum building, designed by Henning Larsen Architects in collaboration with White, has been described as one of the world’s most beautiful university museums.

# Explore the world through design

[20 October 2026\\ \\ **Three questions for Ilona Sagar**\\ \\ We met artist and filmmaker Ilona Sagar and talked about her encounter with the iconic Paimio Sanatorium and why the idea of “care” became so central to the making of her new film work, “Other Actors”. Read more](https://rohsska.se/en/news/three-questions-for-ilona-sagar/)

#### Museum Favourites

## 10 Must-see Highlights

Discover the best of the Röhsska Museum. Here we’ve gathered ten favourites not to miss – from iconic design classics to hidden gems. Perfect if you want to make the most of your visit!

[10 Highlights](https://rohsska.se/en/10-must-see-highlights/)

#### 7 november 2026 – 5 june 2027

## Ilona Sagar: Omsorgens arkitektur

How does architecture shape our health and well-being? Building on Ilona Sagar’s immersive film installation _Other Actors_ (2025), the exhibition explores the links between bodies, health, and architecture through the lens of Aino Marsio-Aalto and Alvar Aalto’s tuberculosis sanatorium in Paimio, Finland. The exhibition takes its title, _Omsorgens arkitektur_, from the Swedish word _omsorg_, referring to an attentive and holistic approach to care.

[Read more](https://rohsska.se/en/exhibitions/ilona-sagar-omsorgens-arkitektur/)

#### Permanent Exhibition

## Design Stories

Everything from the mobile phone in your pocket to the T-shirt you have on or even the font in this text is a result of design. The permanent exhibition Design Stories offers a journey of discovery from the mid-1800s to today with over 500 objects from the museum’s collection. Welcome to a world of design!

[View exhibition](https://rohsska.se/en/exhibitions/design-stories/)

#### Permanent exhibition

## 18th-Century Design & Craft

Dancing figurines, fastidiously ornamented furniture feet and full period interiors. Welcome to 18th-Century Design & Craft, the new permanent exhibition at the Röhsska Museum of Design and Craft.

[View exhibition](https://rohsska.se/en/18th-century-design-craft/)

#### Permanent exhibition

## Inspiration East Asia

The Röhsska Museum’s permanent collection display of applied arts and crafts from Asia reveals the stories and inspirations between the Nordic countries and East Asia.

[read more](https://rohsska.se/en/inspiration-east-asia/)

#### Movie

## Introduction to The Röhsska Museum

We have selected some objects from our collections that in different ways show what the Röhsska Museum is and would like to be.

[Watch here](https://rohsska.se/en/introduction-to-the-museum/)

## **Chairs**

The Röhsska Museum’s collection includes more than 500 chairs. In the open storage repository, visitors can peruse a selection that spans more than 300 years. The chair is an inherently interesting design object that is generally expected to be comfortable, practical and aesthetically pleasing.

[Read more](https://rohsska.se/en/chairs/)

## Torsten och Wanja Söderbergs hall

Read, reflect, discuss. In the Torsten och Wanja Söderbergs hall visitors can immerse themselves in Swedish and Nordic design.

[Read more](https://rohsska.se/en/torsten-och-wanja-soderbergs-hall/)

# Britta Marakatt-Labba

Britta Marakatt-Labba has gained international recognition for her extraordinary embroideries. Her drawings and watercolours, however, are almost entirely unknown – works she has kept out of the public eye until now. The exhibition at The Nordic Watercolour Museum focuses on Britta Marakatt-Labba’s works on paper, which are being shown publicly for the first time. The exhibition features around 140 works, primarily watercolours, drawings and sketches, complemented by a selection of embroideries and graphic works.

[Read more](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/exhibitions/britta-marakatt-labba-en)

[Opening hours:](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/hours-and-admission)

[Admission:](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/hours-and-admission)

## Welcome to the museum!

At The Nordic Watercolour Museum, you can explore current exhibitions, engage in something creative, or take in the breathtaking views of the nearby archipelago on the Swedish West Coast. The museum is a place for all ages – whether you want to experience art, take part in activities, or simply enjoy a peaceful moment by the water. Discover what’s on and plan your visit.

[Visit the museum](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit)

Photo: Per Pixel Petersson

## Upcoming events

- [24 Nov 3.00 PM–5.00 PM\\ \\ **Knit & Stitch**\\ \\ Together with Tjörnslöjd, we invite you to a shared craft session in the exhibition with Britta Marakatt-Labba! Then, we settle down inside the exhibition to work on our own crafts. Bring your own materials, all techniques and expressions are welcome.](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/events/knit-stitch)

- [27 Nov 3.00 PM–9.00 PM\\ \\ **Friday Evening at the Museum – full programme!**\\ \\ On Friday 27 November, we invite you to spend the evening at The Nordic Watercolour Museum! Enjoy late-night opening hours, guided tours of the exhibitions, live performances and a lively atmosphere at Vatten Restaurang & Kafé.](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/events/fridayevening-nov2026)

- [27 Nov 5.30 PM–6.15 PM\\ \\ **Ánndaris Rimpi (Swe/Sápmi)**\\ \\ A live performance by sound artist Ánndaris Rimpi, creating a soundscape in dialogue with Britta Marakatt-Labba’s artworks, performed inside the exhibition at the museum. Admission free, no pre-booking required.](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/events/anndaris-rimpi-en)

Learn more about the art

## Guided tours

Welcome to join our guided tours (in Swedish), held every Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday at 2 pm. The tours are included in the admission fee, and no pre-booking is required. On 14 November, the tour will be interpreted in Swedish Sign Language.

[Guided tours](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/events/guided-tours)

Work in image by Gunnel Wåhlstrand. Photo: Simone Frankel

Current exhibition 27 September 2026–11 April 2027

## Britta Marakatt-Labba

Over the past decade, Britta Marakatt-Labba has made an almost unparalleled breakthrough. Her embroidered narratives revolve around Sámi life in close relationship with nature, but also around colonialism, loss and resistance – about the face of racism, human greed and the lost lands once grazed by the animals. The drawings and watercolours, created largely without any intention of being exhibited publicly, are thematically closely related to her embroideries. Similar motifs recur in the works on paper, but in a new and more intimate form.

[Read more](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/exhibitions/britta-marakatt-labba-en)

Britta Marakatt-Labba, Draft for lithography, commission by Konstfrämjandet, 1990–1992 © Britta Marakatt-Labba / Bildupphovsrätt 2026

Britta Marakatt-Labba, Untitled, 1999 © Britta Marakatt-Labba / Bildupphovsrätt 2026

## This is The Nordic Watercolour Museum

Welcome to The Nordic Watercolour Museum – a vibrant meeting place for art, nature, and creativity by the sea. Here, you can experience contemporary watercolour art, be inspired by our unique setting, or take part in exciting activities for all ages. All year round.

## Discover the museum

- [**Guest studios**\\ \\ THE GUEST STUDIOS are situated on Bockholmen across from the museum. The studios are primarily used for artistic development work, research and study, but may also be hired by others when available.](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/visit/gueststudios)

- [**School**\\ \\ Would you like to visit the museum with your SCHOOL? The Nordic Watercolour Museum is an inquisitive museum that believes in the connection between art and knowledge. We actively engage in educational work through exhibitions and workshops for all ages. A visit to the museum can take many forms. As a class, you can choose to explore the museum independently or accompanied by our art educators.](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/school)

- [**History and architecture**\\ \\ The Nordic Watercolour Museum has been welcoming visitors for 26 years, but the dream of a museum dedicated to watercolour techniques goes back even further. Our HISTORY of how this meeting place for creativity, culture, and nature came to be is filled with passionate individuals, bold visions, and visitor numbers that have exceeded all expectations.](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/about/history)

- [**Friends of the Museum**\\ \\ Did you know the museum has a FRIENDS ASSOCIATION? By becoming a member, you support The Nordic Watercolour Museum and join a community of art enthusiasts. Members enjoy exclusive previews of upcoming exhibitions and receive an annual pass to the museum. Additionally, the association regularly hosts its own events.](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/about/friends-of-the-museum)

Read more about

## The Collection

Unlike many other museums, The Nordic Watercolour Museum does not have a permanent exhibition of works from its collection. Instead, we continuously showcase selections from it. By working solely with temporary exhibitions, we are able to present a larger portion of our collection over time. The collection is a living and vital part of the museum's activities, and you can discover more about it here on our website.

[Read more about the collection](https://www.akvarellmuseet.org/en/the-collection)

Works in image by artist Michael Kvium. Photo: Anna Berglund

## Vatten Restaurang & Kafé

At the restaurant, you can enjoy memorable moments in the midst of a stunning scenery. The chefs cook from scratch; simple dishes with a focus on quality ingredients. The museum and the restaurant operate as separate entities but are united by a shared passion for the unique atmosphere of the location. Learn more about what the restaurant has to offer on their website or by contacting them.

[Website (in Swedish)](https://restaurangvatten.se/)

# The best museums to visit to understand us Danes better

We have a rich history. So rich in fact that most of us can't even retell half of it. But luckily, we have a lot of passionate locals around the country, who are eager to share their vast knowledge of Denmark's history and culture at our many museums. Here are 18 of Denmark’s best museums.

National Gallery of Denmark

Photo: SMK - National Gallery of Denmark

Photo: @nationalmuseet

## Nationalmuseet

Don’t know where to start your journey through Denmark’s history? Then we suggest you head to our National Museum. Get a general overview of the different eras of our history, or immerse yourself in a specific time period. Stone Age, Viking Age, the Middle Ages, Renaissance or Modern times, this museum’s got it all.

[Read moreRead more "Nationalmuseet"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/the-national-museum-gdk410508)

View on mapshow Nationalmuseet on\_map

© Your rainbow panorama, Olafur Eliasson, 2006 - 2011, ARoS Aarhus Art MuseumPhoto: Robin Skjoldborg.

## ARoS

In the centre of our second city, Aarhus, you’ll find one of the largest art museums in Northern Europe, ARoS, and one of our absolute favourites. Because this museum figured out how to make the greyest days colourful, by simply slapping a giant circular rainbow walkway on the top of the building.

[Read moreRead more "ARoS"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/aros-aarhus-art-museum-gdk1077501)

View on mapshow ARoS on\_map

Photo: Lærke Bech Johansen for H.C. Andersen's House

## H.C. Andersens Hus

People tend to say that walking around in our little kingdom is like walking in a fairy tale. This comparison might be due to a certain Danish fairy tale writer whose stories are known around the world. Hans Christian Andersen has given us tales such as The Little Mermaid, The Ugly Duckling and The Snow Queen. And you can get to know our most famous author and his world at H.C.Andersen Hus in Odense. 

[Read moreRead more "H.C. Andersens Hus"](https://hcandersenshus.dk/en/)

View on mapshow H.C. Andersens Hus on\_map

Photo: Bang Clemme Film & Openhouse - Kongernes Jelling

## Kongernes Jelling

Did you know that we can pinpoint when we went from being simply humans living somewhere close to each other to being Danes? We even have a birth certificate in the form of two big Viking rune stones. You can see them in the little town of Jelling and learn more about our Viking kings at the visitor centre, Kongernes Jelling.

[Read moreRead more "Kongernes Jelling"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/kongernes-jelling-home-of-the-viking-kings-gdk608020)

View on mapshow Kongernes Jelling on\_map

Photo: Mike Bink

## Tirpitz

Hidden beneath the dunes along our rugged North Sea coast, you might be able to spot the hidden bunker museum, Tirpitz, which tells the story of the Atlantic Wall during the 2nd World War. But you’ll also get an look inside the history of the entire region, and our relationship with and dependence on the wild North Sea.

[Read moreRead more "Tirpitz"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/tirpitz-gdk609864)

View on mapshow Tirpitz on\_map

Photo: Ulrik Jantzen - Louisiana Museum of Modern Art

## Louisiana Museum of Modern Art

As the first museum of modern art in Denmark, Louisiana was the place where we Danes learned how to appreciate contemporary art. Today, the museum is a leading international art museum and its exhibitions are critically acclaimed. Add to that, it has one of the world’s best locations (in our humble opinion) as you’ll be able to enjoy the incredible view of Øresund.

[Read moreRead more "Louisiana Museum of Modern Art"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/louisiana-museum-of-modern-art-worldclass-art-by-oresund-gdk621156)

View on mapshow Louisiana Museum of Modern Art on\_map

Photo: Rasmus Hjortshøj - Copenhagen Media Center

## M/S Museet for Søfart

We’re a proud little island nation with a long maritime history. Wherever we are in Denmark, we’re never more than 53 km from the sea, which has made us dependent on the sea throughout our history. At the M/S Maritime Museum of Denmark in Helsingør, we’ll tell you about our seafaring Viking raids, sing a few sea shanties, and teach you how to navigate and do trades like it was 1749. 

[Read moreRead more "M/S Museet for Søfart"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/ms-maritime-museum-of-denmark-gdk620757)

View on mapshow M/S Museet for Søfart on\_map

Photo: SMK - National Gallery of Denmark

## SMK - Statens Museum for Kunst

At our National Gallery, you can see how we Danes have depicted our everyday lives throughout the past seven centuries. SMK is particularly known for its comprehensive collections of paintings from the Danish Golden Age and contemporary art pieces. 

[Read moreRead more "SMK - Statens Museum for Kunst"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/smk-the-national-gallery-of-denmark-gdk427321)

View on mapshow SMK - Statens Museum for Kunst on\_map

Photo: Mark Gray

## Frederiksborg Castle

Frederiksborg Castle is one of the most famous castles in Denmark and for good reason: situated on three islands surrounded by a lake and beautiful gardens, it's simply breathtaking. Home to the Museum of National History, the grounds are full of rich history, architecture, and gardens.

[Read moreRead more "Frederiksborg Castle"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/things-do/history-heritage/frederiksborg-castle)

View on mapshow Frederiksborg Castle on\_map

Photo: Kim Wyon

## Designmuseum Danmark

Some say you shouldn’t meet your icons. But when it comes to the Danish design icons, we wouldn’t go without them. We have an enormous passion for design, and after a visit to the Design Museum in Copenhagen, you’ll hopefully understand why. 

[Read moreRead more "Designmuseum Danmark"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/designmuseum-danmark-gdk410498)

View on mapshow Designmuseum Danmark on\_map

© Robin Skjoldborg

## Den Gamle By

Experience how our lives have changed and evolved over the past 400 years by literally walking through history at The Old Town Museum in Aarhus. Walk a street from 1600 and peek into an apartment from the 1970s and watch the world modernise all in one visit. 

[Read moreRead more "Den Gamle By"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/den-gamle-by-the-old-town-museum-in-aarhus-gdk631880)

View on mapshow Den Gamle By on\_map

Photo: Moesgaard Museum

## Moesgaard Museum

If you want to know who we were before we were Danes, we suggest you head to Moesgaard Museum in Aarhus where you can figure out what happened all those many years ago in pre-historic Denmark. (P.S. We love that you’re so interested in our history that you want to take it waaaaaay back!)

[Read moreRead more "Moesgaard Museum"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/moesgaard-museum-gdk603941)

View on mapshow Moesgaard Museum on\_map

Photo: Astrid Maria Rasmussen - Copenhagen Media Center

## The Danish Architecture Center

Our skylines tell us as good a story as our museums these days. And where better to hear about how these buildings were built and why than the Danish Architecture Center? This Copenhagen museum is packed with stories about people and spaces, including sections on everyone from Jørn Utzon, Vilhelm Lauritzen and Arne Jacobsen to modern starchitects like Bjarke Ingels.

[Read moreRead more "The Danish Architecture Center"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/danish-architecture-center-gdk414885)

View on mapshow The Danish Architecture Center on\_map

Photo: Copenhagen Media Center

## Home of Carlsberg

We Danes love beer. And we'd love to share our passion for beer with you. It might happen over a pint in a bar, at a beer tasting at a local brewery, or you could head to the old Carlsberg Brewery in Copenhagen, where you can learn all about our proud history of brewing high-quality beer and Carlsberg, the world's most famous beer company. Probably.

[Read moreRead more "Home of Carlsberg"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/home-of-carlsberg-gdk635356)

View on mapshow Home of Carlsberg on\_map

Photo: Martin Heiberg - Copenhagen Media Center

## Vikingeskibsmuseet

Our little part of the world is known around the world as the home of the Vikings. And this era in our history has put a permanent mark on us Danes – we call Christmas _jul,_ which can be traced back to our Viking ancestors). At our Viking Ship Museum in the historic town of Roskilde, you can learn to set sail and build ships like they did all those years ago. 

[Read moreRead more "Vikingeskibsmuseet"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/the-viking-ship-museum-in-roskilde-gdk660485)

View on mapshow Vikingeskibsmuseet on\_map

Photo: Museumskoncernen ROMU

## Ragnarock

You can tell a lot about a country by studying its songs and musical heritage. And if you’re a music lover like us, we’d love to show and play you some of Denmark’s most iconic and influential songs at the museum for pop, rock and youth culture, Ragnarock. You might even know a few of them. The museum is in the city of Roskilde, which is also home to Northern Europe’s biggest music festival.

[Read moreRead more "Ragnarock"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/the-rock-museum-in-roskilde-gdk912482)

View on mapshow Ragnarock on\_map

Photo: Brittany Overgaard

## Frilandsmuseet

In just one afternoon, you can travel the length and breadth of Denmark at the Open Air Museum, north of Copenhagen. Here you’ll find 50 re-erected farms, mills, and houses which we Danes lived in from the 1600 – 1900s, and you’ll meet passionate reenactors who will show you how we used to spend our lives.

[Read moreRead more "Frilandsmuseet"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/the-open-air-museum-gdk476683)

View on mapshow Frilandsmuseet on\_map

Photo: Skagens Kunstmuseer

## Skagens Museum

At the very top of Denmark’s wild North lies the one of our favourite holiday towns, Skagen. The 700-year-old fishing village transformed into an artsy retreat in the late 1800s, as some of Denmark’s most famous painters flocked to the town to try and capture the area’s unique light. You can see the iconic works of art from the Skagen painters at the Skagen’s Museum.

[Read moreRead more "Skagens Museum"](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/skagens-museum-gdk600081)

View on mapshow Skagens Museum on\_map

View on map

## Want to get even better acquainted with us?

Aww, that’s so sweet of you. And we’re glad. Because we have a lot more stories to tell! Here are a few more suggestions of museums for you to visit.

[Glyptoteket](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/glyptoteket-gdk410562)

Photo: Malin Poppy Darcy Mörner

Glyptoteket

Become an expert on the Danish Golden Age (or pretend you’re in the tropics in the Winter Garden).

Read more

[The Workers' Museum](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/the-workers-museum-gdk410509)

Photo: The Workers' Museum

The Workers' Museum

Walk through an old apartment in Copenhagen, and see how we lived in the past.

Read more

[Denmark's Industrial Museum](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/the-industrial-museum-industrimuseet-gdk608785)

Photo: VisitHorsens

Denmark's Industrial Museum

Figure out how the Industrial Revolution impacted our country and everyday lives.

Read more

[Christiansborg Palace](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/christiansborg-palace-gdk420896)

Photo: Martin Heiberg - Copenhagen Media Center

Christiansborg Palace

Head to our parliament building to learn about our the history of our monarchy and democracy.

Read more

[ARKEN](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/arken-museum-of-contemporary-art-gdk620952)

Photo: Daniel Rasmussen

ARKEN

See how we've expressed ourselves through art from 1990 onwards at the modern art museum, ARKEN.

Read more

[Hammershus Castle Ruins](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/hammershus-gdk614896)

Photo: Nicolas Jægergaard - Destination Bornholm

Hammershus Castle Ruins

Visit the Medieval fortress on Bornholm learn about the island’s history.

Read more

[History Centre Dybbøl Banke](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/historiecenter-dybbol-banke-gdk1084214)

Photo: @senorabubu

History Centre Dybbøl Banke

Explore the battle field of one of Denmark’s most significant wars (but don’t ask us who won…). (Photo: @senorabubu)

Read more

[Kunsten](https://www.visitdenmark.com/denmark/plan-your-trip/kunsten-museum-of-modern-art-aalborg-gdk596128)

Photo: Allan Toft, Kunsten Museum of Modern Art

Kunsten

If you find yourself in the city of Aalborg, head to their art museum, Kunsten. (Photo: Allan Toft, Kunsten)

Read more

# ARoS Aarhus Art Museum

ARoS, Aarhus’ international art museum, invites you to a world of world-class art. Here you can experience works such as Your rainbow panorama and As Seen Below – The Dome, and discover and explore unique collections including 18th-century art – and much more.

[Buy tickets here](https://shop.aros.dk/en/ticket/) [Exhibitions](https://www.aros.dk/en/art/current-exhibitions/)

## A free space for art and creativity

The ARoS collection contains more than 8,000 works, including masterpieces by Danish and international artists.

Some of the most famous works are Olafur Eliasson's [Your rainbow panorama](https://www.visitaarhus.com/aarhus-region/plan-your-trip/your-rainbow-panorama-gdk644165) (2011) and Ron Mueck's oversized sculpture; [Boy](https://www.aros.dk/en/art/the-collection/ron-mueck-boy-1999/) (1999).

## As Seen Below - The Dome, a Skyspace by James Turrell

From 19 June 2026, you can also experience _As Seen Below_, light artist James Turrell's largest Skyspace in a museum context. The monumental installation will cement ARoS' position as one of the world's leading museums for installation art.

[Read more here](https://www.aros.dk/en/art/upcoming-exhibitions/as-seen-below-the-dome-a-skyspace-by-james-turrell/).

## Exhibitions and international perspective

Each year, ARoS presents six to eight major exhibitions with an accompanying programme of public lectures, debates and events. ARoS' international outlook and innovative approach has led to groundbreaking exhibitions with artists such as J.W.M. Turner, Claude Monet, Edvard Munch, Franciska Clausen, Salvador Dalí, Asger Jorn, Per Kirkeby, Barbara Kruger, Isaac Julien, Jenny Holzer, Bill Viola, Mariko Mori, Cindy Sherman and Sarah Sze.

## Art experiences for everyone

More than 600,000 visitors come to ARoS every year for artistic experiences, to shop in the ARoS Store, dine in the ARoS Café and Orangery or simply enjoy its iconic architecture and location.

[See the programme here](https://www.aros.dk/en/art/current-exhibitions/aros-collection-installation-art/).

### Practical information

ARoS is located in the heart of Aarhus and has entrances from Aros Allé/Vester Allé and via Officerspladsen.

- Parking: Parking is available on [Aros Allé](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Park+Zone+-+Aros/@56.1542924,10.1986545,16z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x464c3f92d0e4f6db:0x64c4ec943be836c7!8m2!3d56.1542924!4d10.1986545!16s%2Fg%2F11dxl2xphz?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MTIwMi4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D), where the museum has 79 parking spaces.
- The museum is closed on Mondays, except for Mondays in June, July, August and September, as well as on certain public holidays.
- Admission is always free for everyone under the age of 18.
- Accessibility: The museum has a lift leading up to the entrance beneath the stairs on Aros Allé, as well as lifts to all exhibition galleries and _Your rainbow panorama_. Disabled toilets are available on Levels 3, 4 and 8, as well as on Level 9 in the Roof Pavilion.
- Wheelchairs are available on loan upon request at the Information Desk at ARoS.

# Welcome to Sweden’s most beautiful art museum!

## Opening Hours

Tuesday – Sunday: 11 am – 5 pm

Thursday: 11 am – 8 pm

Monday: Closed

[Holidays and other special opening hours](https://waldemarsudde.se/en/priser-och-oppettider/)

## Admission

Adults SEK 170 
Seniors/students SEK 150 
Groups of 10 or more SEK 150/pp 
Children up to 19 free

Annual card SEK 450

You can purchase your ticket online or onsite at the museum. Payment by card only (VISA and Mastercard accepted). Please note that pre-purchased tickets do not give priority in queue.

[Buy Ticket](https://secure.tickster.com/en/9fvzm1wm8xacpbh/selectevent)

## Visiting Address

Prins Eugens väg 6 
Djurgården, Stockholm

[How to get here](https://waldemarsudde.se/en/#)

## Current Exhibitions

[Wonderful Colour – Gothenburg Colourism in a New Light\\ \\ Saturday 3/10 2026  –  Sunday 28/2 2027](https://waldemarsudde.se/en/exhibitions/the-wonder-of-colours-gothenburg-colourism-in-a-new-light/) [Landscapes from Near and Far – Works from the Museum’s Collections\\ \\ Sunday 4/10 2026  –  Sunday 15/8 2027](https://waldemarsudde.se/en/exhibitions/landscapes-from-near-and-far-works-from-the-museums-collections/) [Flowers in Fine Art and Decorative Arts – Works from the Museum’s Collections\\ \\ Sunday 4/10 2026  –  Sunday 15/8 2027](https://waldemarsudde.se/en/exhibitions/flowers-in-fine-art-and-decorative-arts-works-from-the-museums-collections/)

## Garden and Sculpture Park

”Second to the arts, I think flowers are my greatest joy,” Prince Eugen wrote in a letter in 1901.

A visit to the beautiful park and garden at Waldemarsudde is a treat for many senses and offers more than a century old garden history. The design of the garden determined by Prince Eugen, is still managed according to the Prince’s instructions and directions.

The park is also rich in sculptures, all of them bought by Prince Eugen, often with specific sites in mind.

[Read more](https://waldemarsudde.se/en/park-and-garden/)

## Prince Eugen’s Art Collection

Prince Eugen was an art collector of note, with special emphasis on Nordic and French art. The Collections number around 7,000 works and comprise painting, sculpture and crafts objects.

The Painting Collection includes works by Ernst Josephson, Anders Zorn, Julia Beck, Isaac Grünewald, Sigrid Hjertén and Sven X:et Erixson. International artists such as Edvard Munch and Auguste Rodin are also represented.

Throughout the year, a selection of Prince Eugen’s own art and works from the Collections, are on display.

[Read more](https://waldemarsudde.se/en/about-waldemarsudde/prince-eugens-art-collection-2/)

## The Museum Shop

In the Museum Shop, you will find exhibition catalogues, a wide selection of art- and garden books, postcards, reproductions and other objects related to the museum, as the popular flowerpot WALDEMARSUDDEKRUKAN®, designed by Prince Eugen himself.

The Museum Shop has the same opening hours as the museum. It is also possible to order items in our webshop.

[Visit the Museum Shop](https://waldemarsudde.se/en/the-museum-shop/)

## Restaurant and Café

The Prince’s Kitchen, situated in the museum, serves hot meals, beverages and delicious pasteries.

Café Ektorpet, situated in the park, offers waffles, a selection of lunch dishes, sandwiches and pastries.

[Read more](https://waldemarsudde.se/en/restaurant-cafe/)

## Explore Prince Eugen’s Waldemarsudde

Free to visit

Rainy days

Hugh Lane Gallery is temporarily closing for refurbishment.

The Hugh Lane Gallery, located on Parnell Square North, Dublin City, houses one of Ireland's most exciting collections of modern and contemporary Irish and international art. Established in 1908, Hugh Lane became the home of artist Francis Bacon’s perfectly preserved studio in 1998. The gallery is free to visit.

The Hugh Lane Gallery, Parnell Square, Dublin, is a must for art lovers. See Impressionist paintings by Manet, Monet, Degas, Pissarro and Morisot, as well as the stunning Francis Bacon Studio. Enjoy the wonderful, wide-ranging collection of Irish art, and the stained glass room displaying Harry Clarke’s gorgeous masterpiece, The Eve of Saint Agnes. Meet some of the famous Irish personalities in portraiture, including WB Yeats who wrote five poems about the gallery.

The diverse and extensive contemporary collections include the Sean Scully Gallery, one of the most beautiful rooms dedicated to the work of a contemporary artist in Europe.

Francis Bacon’s legendary studio was relocated from London to Dublin in 1998 and is permanently on display, preserved exactly as it was. You will find fascinating unfinished works by Francis Bacon, items from his studio, an audio-visual room and touch screens allowing you a deeper look into the life and art of one of the most important figurative artists of the 20th century.

Hugh Lane Gallery is situated in beautiful Charlemont House built in 1763 by the 1st Earl of Charlemont, James Caulfeild. Designed by Sir William Chambers, it still retains many of its original architectural features which complement the works on exhibition.

Facilities include a bookshop and café. There is full wheelchair access and two designated disability parking spaces located directly outside the gallery.

The gallery regularly has temporary exhibitions and new displays from its collections. It also has public tours of the gallery and workshops for children and adults. Sunday concerts are a tradition at the gallery. Check the website for more details.

Why we like it

- The Hugh Lane Gallery's extensive collection is a must for art lovers and is free.
- Francis Bacon's studio is preserved exactly as it was, showing how clutter and chaos spurred his creativity.
- Harry Clarke's stained glass masterpiece is a visual feast of rich colours.
- Offers workshops, children's activities, concerts and temporary exhibitions.

Tips from locals

The Sundays @ Noon Concert Series take place in the beautiful Sculpture Gallery from September to June, admission is free.

jsonLd.name: Hugh Lane Gallery
jsonLd.description:
The Hugh Lane Gallery, located on Parnell Square North, Dublin City, houses one of Ireland's most exciting collections of modern and contemporary Irish and international art. Established in 1908, Hugh Lane became the home of artist Francis Bacon’s perfectly preserved studio in 1998. The gallery is free to visit.

The Hugh Lane Gallery, Parnell Square, Dublin, is a must for art lovers. See Impressionist paintings by Manet, Monet, Degas, Pissarro and Morisot, as well as the stunning Francis Bacon Studio. Enjoy the wonderful, wide-ranging collection of Irish art, and the stained glass room displaying Harry Clarke’s gorgeous masterpiece, The Eve of Saint Agnes. Meet some of the famous Irish personalities in portraiture, including WB Yeats who wrote five poems about the gallery. 

The diverse and extensive contemporary collections include the Sean Scully Gallery, one of the most beautiful rooms dedicated to the work of a contemporary artist in Europe. 

Francis Bacon’s legendary studio was relocated from London to Dublin in 1998 and is permanently on display, preserved exactly as it was. You will find fascinating unfinished works by Francis Bacon, items from his studio, an audio-visual room and touch screens allowing you a deeper look into the life and art of one of the most important figurative artists of the 20th century.

Hugh Lane Gallery is situated in beautiful Charlemont House built in 1763 by the 1st Earl of Charlemont, James Caulfeild. Designed by Sir William Chambers, it still retains many of its original architectural features which complement the works on exhibition.

Facilities include a bookshop and café. There is full wheelchair access and two designated disability parking spaces located directly outside the gallery.

The gallery regularly has temporary exhibitions and new displays from its collections. It also has public tours of the gallery and workshops for children and adults. Sunday concerts are a tradition at the gallery. Check the website for more details.

# Sweden's key modern museums – from north to south

Discover Sweden’s modern and contemporary art museums, where everything from photography and design to painting and sculpture takes centre stage. From Kiruna in the north to Malmö in the south, you'll find inspiring collections, bold exhibitions and distinctive museum settings.

Last updated 20 October 2026

View map

Maps require approval for third-party cookies (Targeting) from Google. Modify cookie settings by clicking the icon at the bottom left. Click "Show map once", to accept Google's [terms](https://policies.google.com/terms) once.

Show map once

Sweden has a vibrant art scene, showcasing both internationally acclaimed artists and emerging talent. Many of the country’s modern museums are attractions in their own right, housed in striking buildings or set in unexpected locations. Here’s our guide to some of Sweden’s standout museums and art spaces, taking you on a cultural journey from north to south.

Kiruna's new city centre

Kiruna’s new city centre, featuring the town hall ‘Kristallen’ and modern Arctic architecture.

Photo: Håkan Stenlund/Swedish Lapland

Show image informationi

## Kin Museum, Kiruna

Located in the striking Kristallen City Hall in [Kiruna](https://visitsweden.com/where-to-go/northern-sweden/norrbotten/kiruna/)’s new city centre, [Kin Museum](https://kinmuseum.se/en) is Sweden’s northernmost art museum. With the Barents region as its starting point, it showcases contemporary art in all its forms, from painting and photography to sculpture and installations. Alongside changing exhibitions, the museum has a growing collection of its own. To spark creativity, it also offers free Saturday art workshops, where children and adults can try their hand at painting, drawing and other creative activities.

Art Friday at Bildmuseet in Umeå

Art Friday at Bildmuseet in Umeå brings people together for an evening of art, music and socialising in a relaxed setting.

Photo: Mikael Lundgren/Bildmuseet

Show image informationi

## Bildmuseet, Umeå

Set beside the Ume River on Umeå Arts Campus, [Bildmuseet](https://www.bildmuseet.umu.se/en/) is one of Sweden’s leading venues for international contemporary art. Part of Umeå University, the museum occupies a striking seven-storey building with a wooden façade, offering exhibitions spanning art, photography, design and architecture. Beyond the exhibitions, Bildmuseet hosts talks, workshops and occasional Art Friday events, ranging from exhibition openings and film screenings to quizzes and live music.

Uppsala Castle

Uppsala Castle was built by Gustav Vasa in the mid 1500's. It has played an important role in Swedish history and housed the Hall of States for a long time. This is where the abbdication of Queen Christina was announced by the Swedish government in 1654.

Photo: Mark Harris/imagebank.sweden.se

Show image informationi

## Uppsala Art Museum, Uppsala

Housed in historic Uppsala Castle, [Uppsala Art Museum](https://konstmuseum.uppsala.se/en) brings together some 14,000 works of art and design, from paintings and sculptures to installations and video art. With a focus on art from the late 19th century to today, the museum presents both works from its own collection and temporary exhibitions. Families can explore the art with specially designed activities for children, while Art Night events bring together guided tours, creative workshops, food, drinks and music.

Stockholm Slides at Moderna Museet

Stockholm Slides by Carsten Höller at Moderna Museet offers a playful way to experience art, with sweeping views across Stockholm’s waterfront from the rooftop.

Photo: My Matson/Moderna Museet

Show image informationi

## Moderna Museet, Stockholm

Set on the island of Skeppsholmen in central Stockholm, [Moderna Museet](https://www.modernamuseet.se/stockholm/en/) is one of Europe’s leading museums of modern and contemporary art. Its impressive collection of over 140,000 works includes paintings, sculptures, photography and film by artists such as Picasso and Dalí. Don’t miss Stockholm Slides, Carsten Höller’s playful artwork featuring two slides that whisk visitors from the museum’s rooftop to ground level (closed during the colder months). The building also houses ArkDes, Sweden’s national museum of architecture and design.

Fotografiska, Stockholm

A waterfront dining experience at Fotografiska’s restaurant in Stockholm, combining seasonal cuisine with striking views and photography exhibitions.

Photo: Julia Donka/Visit Stockholm

Show image informationi

## Fotografiska, Stockholm

Since opening in Stockholm in 2010, [Fotografiska](https://stockholm.fotografiska.com/en) has expanded to cities including Berlin, Tallinn, Shanghai and Shenzhen. Located on Södermalm, this photography museum has no permanent collection, instead presenting changing exhibitions by established and emerging photographers from around the world. Open until late in the evening, it also hosts talks and events. Round off your visit at the award-winning restaurant, serving seasonal food with panoramic views across the water.

Artipelag, Stockholm archipelago

Artipelag, the great art hall in the Stockholm archipelago in Sweden, got its name from the words Art, Activities, and Archipelago. It is a new international venue for art, good food, events, meetings and activities – beautifully set on Värmdö in the Stockholm Archipelago, just 30 minutes from the city centre.

Photo: Jesus Roger/Artipelag/imagebank.sweden.se

Show image informationi

## Artipelag, Stockholm archipelago

Just 30 minutes from central Stockholm, [Artipelag](https://artipelag.se/en/) brings together art, design, food and nature in a striking waterfront setting on Värmdö island. Its name combines ‘art’ and ‘archipelago’, reflecting its location in the Stockholm archipelago. The purpose-built museum hosts changing exhibitions, while large windows frame views of the surrounding forest and sea. Explore the outdoor sculpture park or enjoy a meal overlooking the water. On weekends, a direct bus connects Artipelag with central Stockholm.

Röda Sten Konsthall, Gothenburg

Röda Sten is an art and culture centre in Gothenburg that strives to widen the definition of art. The building that houses Röda Sten was originally a boiler house for the local industries.

Photo: Joachim Brink/imagebank.sweden.se

Show image informationi

## Röda Sten Konsthall, Gothenburg

Housed in a former boiler house beneath the Älvsborg Bridge in Gothenburg, [Röda Sten Konsthall](https://rodastenkonsthall.se/en/) has a colourful past. Once a venue for rave parties and threatened with demolition, the industrial building is now a hub for contemporary art, showcasing sculpture, installations, photography and video art. The gallery also hosts talks and workshops and organises the [Gothenburg International Biennial for Contemporary Art](https://www.gibca.se/en/) (GIBCA), held across the city. The next edition runs from 4 September to 21 November 2027.

Borås Konstmuseum, West Sweden

Petra Bauer’s Women in Movement at Borås Art Biennial 2026, presented at Borås Konstmuseum.

Photo: Petra Bauer/Borås Konstmuseum

Show image informationi

## Borås Konstmuseum, Borås

With a focus on contemporary and public art, [Borås Konstmuseum](https://boraskonstmuseum.se/english/boras-museum-of-modern-art.html) showcases Swedish and international artists through painting, sculpture, photography and moving images. Admission is free, and visitors can explore exhibitions, guided tours and creative activities. Since 2008, the museum has organised the Borås International Sculpture Biennial, with the next edition in 2028. Beyond the museum, use its digital art map to discover sculptures, murals and other public artworks around the city – and see why Borås is known as ‘the sculpture city’.

Hallands Konstmuseum in Halmstad

Hallands Konstmuseum in Halmstad combines a distinctive 1930s brick building with modern extensions, housing exhibitions of art from Halland and beyond.

Photo: Hallands konstmuseum/Visit Halland

Show image informationi

## Hallands Konstmuseum, Halmstad

Set beside the Nissan River in central Halmstad, [Hallands Konstmuseum](https://hallandskonstmuseum.se/en/) occupies a distinctive 1930s building designed by architect Ragnar Hjorth. The museum houses an extensive and growing collection of art from Halland and beyond, including works by the renowned Halmstad Group, pioneers of Swedish surrealism. Several exhibitions run alongside each other, often drawing on the museum’s own collection, while weekend guided tours (included in the admission fee) offer a chance to explore the art in greater depth.

Moderna Museet, Malmö

Moderna Museet is one of Europe’s leading museums of modern and contemporary art. It also includes the colourful Moderna Caféet.

Photo: Miriam Preis/imagebank.sweden.se

Show image informationi

## Moderna Museet, Malmö

Opened in 2009 as a branch of Stockholm’s renowned [Moderna Museet](https://www.modernamuseet.se/en/malmo/), the Malmö museum showcases modern and contemporary art by Swedish and international artists, drawing on the museum’s extensive collection alongside temporary exhibitions. Housed in a former power station with a striking orange-red extension, it’s just a 10-minute walk from Malmö Central Station. Beyond the exhibitions, there’s a varied programme for all ages, from baby painting and creative workshops to Drink & Draw sessions and peaceful mornings at the museum.

Malmö Konsthall, Skåne

Installation view of In the City Grows a Field – 50 Artists in Malmö, an exhibition at Malmö Konsthall in 2022.

Photo: Helene Toresdotter/Malmö Konsthall

Show image informationi

## Malmö Konsthall, Malmö

One of the Nordic region’s largest venues for contemporary art, [Malmö Konsthall](https://malmokonsthall.se/en/) opened in 1975 in a distinctive box-like building designed by architect Klas Anshelm. Located in central Malmö, near Triangeln shopping centre, the gallery presents three to four exhibitions a year, featuring Swedish and international artists. Its varied programme also includes literature, music, film, performing arts and debates. Admission to all exhibitions and events is free, making it easy to drop in and discover something new.

# En plats för konstmöten 
och oväntade upplevelser

Varmt välkommen till Norrköpings Konstmuseum! Museet har en av Sveriges främsta konstsamlingar inom modernism och samtidskonst. Dessutom har museet en omfattande grafiksamling och en grönskande skulpturpark som är en lugn oas mitt i staden. Konstmuseet har fri entré till galleri  1 och 2.

### KONSTMUSEETS KAFÉ ÖPPET LÖRDAGAR OCH SÖNDAGAR

Kaféet är öppet lördagar och söndagar under museets ordinarie öppettider under hösten. Här serveras kaffe och te samt bakverk efter säsong.

# Swedish heritage & history

Sweden’s past is proudly on show across the country, with 15 UNESCO World Heritage Sites and countless museums – there’s something for every history or culture-loving traveller.

## **Explore Sweden’s cultural treasures**

With 15 UNESCO-listed sites, Sweden ranks among the world’s top cultural heritage destinations. These landmarks are spread from north to south, offering your clients plenty of options to add a historic highlight to their itinerary.

In Swedish Lapland, the **Gammelstad Church Town** in Luleå is a must-see. This charming village of 424 red wooden cottages once gave overnight shelter to rural churchgoers. In Hälsingland, east-central Sweden, visitors can explore richly decorated wooden farmhouses, famous for their intricate folk art and a deep connection to rural traditions.

The **rock carvings of Tanum**, on the West Coast near Bohuslän, provide a fascinating glimpse into Bronze Age life, while the **Royal Domain of Drottningholm** – just outside Stockholm – offers grandeur, history and UNESCO-listed gardens. Visitors can explore the royal palace, the Chinese Pavilion and an 18th-century theatre that’s still in use today.

In southern Sweden, **Karlskrona’s naval port** showcases Sweden’s maritime legacy. Built in 1680, this UNESCO site was designed for constructing warships and remains a captivating destination for fans of naval and military history.

Off the southeast coast lies **Öland**, an island of sweeping landscapes and historic villages, linked to the mainland by a six-kilometre bridge from Kalmar. Nearby, the island of **Gotland** is equally rich in heritage. The medieval town of Visby is encircled by a 3.5-kilometre stone wall dating back to the 12th century. Each August, the town comes alive with jousting, crafts and costumes during Medieval Week (‘Medeltidsveckan’) – a brilliant time to visit for clients keen on immersive history.

## **Swedish museums – dynamic, authentic, and full of surprises (including great food)**

#### **Museum must-visits in Stockholm**

Stockholm is home to some of Sweden’s most iconic museums. On the island of Djurgården, the [**Vasa Museum**](https://www.vasamuseet.se/en) – Sweden and Scandinavia’s most visited – tells the dramatic story of the 17th-century warship that sank on her maiden voyage and was later salvaged almost entirely intact.

Nearby, visitors can dive into Swedish pop history at the [**ABBA Museum**](https://abbathemuseum.com/en/), or explore the life and legacy of global music icon Avicii at **The Avicii Experience**, part of the immersive SPACE digital culture centre. At **Tekniska museet** (the Swedish National Museum of Science and Technology), the new 360-degree [**Wisdome**](https://www.tekniskamuseet.se/en/wisdome/) dome experience brings science to life in a big, bold way.

For younger visitors, [**Junibacken**](https://www.junibacken.se/en/) is a wonderland dedicated to Astrid Lindgren’s beloved stories – including the ever-popular Pippi Longstocking (‘Pippi Långstrump’). But no matter which museum your clients choose, children are well catered for. Most museums in Sweden offer family-friendly exhibitions and activities as standard.

#### **Museums with a view (and a walk or cycle)**

On the west coast, the island of Tjörn is home to **Pilane**, an [open-air sculpture park](https://www.pilane.org/en/index.php) set among ancient grazing lands – a unique combination of nature, art and history. Just a scenic cycle away is the **Nordic Watercolour Museum**, right by the water’s edge.

Further north, in the heart of Swedish Lapland, **Arjeplog’s Silver Museum** traces 10,000 years of history, culture and craftsmanship through stunning examples of Sámi silverwork.

#### **Cultural experiences that won’t cost a thing**

Many museums in Sweden are free to enter, especially for younger visitors. Some highlights include:

- [**Malmö Konsthall**](https://www.konsthall.malmo.se/en/valkommen/) – one of Sweden’s largest contemporary art spaces
- [**Gothenburg Museum of Art**](https://goteborgskonstmuseum.se/en/visit-the-museum/) – free for visitors under 20
- [**Nationalmuseum**](https://www.nationalmuseum.se/en) in Stockholm – free for visitors under 20
- [**Moderna Museet**](https://www.modernamuseet.se/stockholm/en/), Stockholm – a modern and contemporary art gem on the island of Skeppsholmen

#### **Explore the world’s longest art gallery – with just a metro ticket**

With a day pass for the **Stockholm metro**, your clients can explore 110 km of underground art. Each station features unique artworks – murals, mosaics, installations and sculptures – turning the daily commute into a cultural adventure. Highlights include **Kungsträdgården** station, where the design references local plant life and the former 17th-century palace, _Makalös_, that once stood nearby.

And best of all – it’s one of the most sustainable ways to explore the city.

Limerick City Gallery of Art in Limerick City, invites you to see the best of contemporary art through the temporary exhibition programme and to enjoy the permanent collection of 19th and 20th century Irish art.

Limerick City Gallery of Art LCGA in Limerick City, is one of the leading contemporary art galleries in Ireland and is home to an important collection of Irish 18th to 21st century art in all media. It has the National Collection of Contemporary Drawing and the Michael O’Connor International Poster Collection part of its collections. The Permanent Collection is exhibited on a rotation basis throughout the year in its dedicated exhibition gallery.

Artists within the Permanent Collection are Paul Henry, Jack B. Yeats, Sean Keating, Charles Lamb, Letita Hamilton, Grace Henry, Sarah Purser, Walter Verling, Donald Teskey, John Shinnors, and many more. LCGA hosts around 8 contemporary exhibits per year with Irish and International artists and hosts EVA International, Ireland's biennial of contemporary art.

LCGA is housed in the Carnegie Building, on the grounds of the People’s Park in the centre of Limerick City. Limerick City Gallery of Art is fully accessible with a ramp at the front entrance, wide doorways, a lift and disabled toilet facilities.

jsonLd.name: Limerick City Gallery of Art
jsonLd.description:
Limerick City Gallery of Art LCGA in Limerick City, is one of the leading contemporary art galleries in Ireland and is home to an important collection of Irish 18th to 21st century art in all media. It has the National Collection of Contemporary Drawing and the Michael O’Connor International Poster Collection part of its collections. The Permanent Collection is exhibited on a rotation basis throughout the year in its dedicated exhibition gallery.

Artists within the Permanent Collection are Paul Henry, Jack B. Yeats, Sean Keating, Charles Lamb, Letita Hamilton, Grace Henry, Sarah Purser, Walter Verling, Donald Teskey, John Shinnors, and many more. LCGA hosts around 8 contemporary exhibits per year with Irish and International artists and hosts EVA International, Ireland's biennial of contemporary art.

LCGA is housed in the Carnegie Building, on the grounds of the People’s Park in the centre of Limerick City. Limerick City Gallery of Art is fully accessible with a ramp at the front entrance, wide doorways, a lift and disabled toilet facilities.
jsonLd.disambiguatingDescription: Limerick City Gallery of Art in Limerick City, invites you to see the best of contemporary art through the temporary exhibition programme and to enjoy the permanent collection of 19th and 20th century Irish art.

# 10 cultural sites not to be missed during your stay in Paris

Inspiration

ParisCultural HeritageCities

© Getty Images

Reading time: 0 minPublished on 18 June 2013, updated on 16 October 2023

Votre séjour à Paris sera l'occasion de découvrir une capitale en perpétuelle effervescence. Ville Lumière, Paris est aussi un musée à ciel ouvert hors du commun dans lequel de nombreux sites culturels constituent des immanquables ! Pour vous aider dans votre choix de lieux et musées à ne pas manquer, découvrez le top 10 des sites parisiens incontournables, à voir absolument pendant votre séjour !

Your trip to Paris is a chance to get to know a capital in constant motion. City of Light, Paris is also an open-air museum with countless cultural sites that are well worth a visit!

To help you choose from the long list of unmissable monuments and museums, here are the top ten Parisian must-sees:

- The **Eiffel Tower**and Champ de Mars
- The **Louvre Museum**
- The **Musée d’Orsay**
- The **Centre Pompidou**
- The **Palace of Versailles**
- The **Sacré-Coeur Basilica**
- The **Notre-Dame Cathedral**
- The **Arc de Triomphe**
- The **Quai Branly Museum**
- The **Grand Palais Galleries**

## Le Musée du Louvre, l'un des plus grands musées du monde

Idéalement situé au cœur de Paris, le long de la Seine, le musée du Louvre a pour écrin l’ancien palais des rois de France. Toutefois, depuis 1989, ce monument est aussi reconnaissable à la grande pyramide, qui a pris place dans sa cour principale, et qui constitue son entrée principale. À tel point que ce joyau de verre est devenu le symbole du Louvre lui-même. Mais au-delà de l’architecture de ce bâtiment, c’est bien aussi son incroyable collection d’œuvres d’art qui mérite le détour. En effet, ce musée universel expose, dans ses huit départements, plus de 30 000 œuvres traversant les siècles et les civilisations, et un nombre exceptionnel de chefs-d’œuvre mondialement connus (sculptures, peintures, objets d’art...). Pour n’en citer que quelques-uns : le Scribe accroupi, la Vénus de Milo, Les Captifs de Michel-Ange, La Joconde de Vinci, Les Noces de Cana de Véronèse, L’Astronome de Vermeer, La Liberté guidant le peuple de Delacroix... [Musée du Louvre](https://www.louvre.fr/)

## Le Musée d’Orsay et sa riche collection d'art impressionniste

De l’autre côté de la Seine (côté rive gauche), quasiment en face du Louvre, se déploie ce musée qui prend place dans un bâtiment atypique : une ancienne gare parisienne d’une rare élégance, édifiée par le célèbre architecte Victor Laloux pour accueillir en plein cœur de Paris les visiteurs lors de l’exposition universelle de 1900. Quant à sa collection, elle se révèle tout aussi exceptionnelle. En effet, le musée d’Orsay dévoile la plus grande collection d’œuvres impressionnistes du monde, comptant de multiples chefs-d’œuvre datant de la 2NDE moitié du XIXe siècle au début du XXe. Vous pourrez notamment y admirer des œuvres incontournables de Gustave Courbet, d’Édouard Manet, de Degas, d’Auguste Renoir, de Vincent Van Gogh, de Claude Monet, d’Auguste Rodin… mais également une superbe collection d’arts décoratifs et de sculptures. [Musée d’Orsay](https://www.musee-orsay.fr/fr)

## Le Centre Pompidou et son architecture unique

Mondialement connu pour son architecture avant-gardiste, ce bâtiment, construit en plein cœur du quartier des Halles de Paris, ne laisse pas indifférent. D’autant que cette construction atypique offre à ses visiteurs d’incroyables vues sur les toits et les monuments de Paris, grâce à ses escaliers mécaniques recouverts de tubes de Plexiglas permettant de relier les 6 étages du musée. Car, en effet, ce monument abrite l’un des plus fascinants musées d’art moderne et contemporain d’Europe, comptant plus de 100 000 œuvres, datant des XXe et XXIe siècles. Les grands domaines artistiques de cette période y sont d’ailleurs représentés depuis le dessin jusqu’aux nouveaux médias, en passant par les arts plastiques, la photographie, l’architecture, le design ou encore le cinéma. La collection compte d’ailleurs une liste impressionnante d’artistes célèbres : Picasso, Matisse, Braque, Léger, Kandinsky, Delaunay, Giacometti, Dubuffet… De quoi découvrir ou redécouvrir les mouvements artistiques de l’art moderne (qu’il s’agisse du cubisme, du surréalisme ou des abstractions). [Centre Pompidou](https://www.centrepompidou.fr/fr/)

> [Voir cette publication sur Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/CztrPQ_BPSg/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
> 
> [Une publication partagée par Centre Pompidou (@centrepompidou)](https://www.instagram.com/p/CztrPQ_BPSg/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

## Le Château de Versailles et ses jardins somptueux

Également incontournable à visiter lorsqu’on est sur la capitale, le château de Versailles permet de passer en revue tout un pan de l’Histoire de France, depuis Louis XIV jusqu’à Louis XVI. En effet, cet imposant bâtiment à l’architecture impressionnante a été pendant plus d’un siècle la résidence principale des rois de France. Pourquoi visiter ce château ? Pour admirer son joyau : la galerie des Glaces (longue de 7 mètres de longs et parée de près de 360 miroirs). Pour revivre le quotidien du roi et de la reine en admirant leurs appartements, mais aussi pour découvrir le domaine du Trianon (refuge de Marie-Antoinette). Ou encore pour savourer la beauté de ses jardins créés par Le Nôtre, que ce soit de jour comme de nuit, notamment à l’occasion du festival des Grandes Eaux Musicales ou des Grandes Eaux Nocturnes. [Château de Versailles](https://www.chateauversailles.fr/)

## La Basilique du Sacré-Cœur et sa vue panoramique sur la ville

Prenant place au sommet de la butte Montmartre, soit à plus de 130 mètres de hauteur, cet édifice religieux à l’architecture d’inspiration romane et byzantine accorde à ses visiteurs l’un des plus exceptionnels panoramas de Paris. Pour accéder au bâtiment, deux options s’offrent à vous : la montée des célèbres escaliers de la butte ou l’emprunt du funiculaire du quartier. Une fois à l’intérieur, plusieurs ouvrages d’exception attirent l’attention : l’une des plus grandes mosaïques du monde (de 475 m²), le son de la plus grande cloche de France, mais surtout son dôme dont l’accès extérieur (par 300 marches) délivre une splendide vue sur la ville. Profitez aussi de votre visite pour parcourir le quartier environnant : la célèbre place du Tertre et ses artistes, mais aussi le quartier des Abbesses aux ruelles si inspirantes. [Basilique du Sacré-Cœur](https://www.sacre-coeur-montmartre.com/)

## La Cathédrale Notre-Dame, chef d’œuvre de l’architecture gothique

S’élevant fièrement sur l’île de la Cité, en plein cœur de Paris, depuis le XIIe siècle, Notre-Dame-de-Paris ne cesse d’émerveiller. En effet, même si le bâtiment a été fortement endommagé par l’incendie de 2019, et s’avère actuellement fermé au public, sa façade et ses tours ornées de dentelle de pierre, dans le plus pur style gothique, ainsi que ces splendides vitraux et rosaces ont résisté. Ce monument continue donc d’enchanter ses spectateurs par ses prouesses architecturales, comme il a inspiré Victor Hugo pour l’écriture de son chef-d’œuvre, Notre-Dame-de-Paris. En attendant sa réouverture prévue pour décembre 2024, les visiteurs peuvent profiter d’une exposition gratuite sur le parvis de la cathédrale, consacrée à la restauration du monument et mettant en valeur le savoir-faire des artisans sollicités, intitulée « Notre-Dame de Paris : Au cœur du chantier ». [Notre-Dame-de-Paris](https://www.notredamedeparis.fr/)

## L'Arc de Triomphe, le plus grand arc du monde

Érigé à l’extrémité de « la plus belle avenue du monde », Les Champs-Élysées, ce monument a un fort pouvoir symbolique. En effet, la construction de ce monument, initiée Napoléon Ier, sous l’Empire, pour commémorer la victoire de la bataille d’Austerlitz, sert depuis à célébrer la grandeur de la France et à rendre hommage au courage des soldats français devant l’adversité. Hommage rendu plus vif par la présence de la tombe du Soldat inconnu installée sous cet arc depuis le 11 novembre 1920. Mais la visite de ce site culturel (et de son musée) n’a pas comme seul intérêt de rappeler des moments clé de l’Histoire de la France. En effet, la terrasse de cet édifice offre également aux touristes un superbe panorama sur le Paris haussmannien, notamment sur cet axe incroyable qui relie la Grande Arche de la Défense au nord-ouest à l’obélisque de la place de la Concorde et au musée du Louvre au centre de la capitale. [Arc de Triomphe](https://www.paris-arc-de-triomphe.fr/)

## Le Musée du Quai Branly dédié aux arts et civilisations non-occidentaux

Jouissant d’un emplacement de choix, à proximité de la tour Eiffel, ce musée séduit en tout premier lieu par son architecture (création de Jean Nouvel) qui accorde une place de choix à la nature, en plein cœur de Paris. Mais une fois franchies ses portes et sa fameuse rivière de mots, ce sont bien ses milliers d’œuvres d'Afrique, d'Asie, d'Océanie et des Amériques non occidentales qui happent le public. Cette incroyable collection emmène, en effet, les visiteurs dans un immense voyage à travers l’histoire, la culture, les religions des autres continents, de l’antiquité à nos jours. L’un des atouts majeurs du musée : ses nombreuses animations dédiées aux enfants et aux familles (visites contées, ateliers musicaux, artistiques…). [Musée du Quai Branly](https://www.quaibranly.fr/fr/)

> [Voir cette publication sur Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/CYozwYcoUOy/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)
> 
> [Une publication partagée par musée du quai Branly (@quaibranly)](https://www.instagram.com/p/CYozwYcoUOy/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

## Les Galeries du Grand Palais, qui ont révélé de grands artistes au public.

Doté d’une architecture d’une rare élégance, ce monument a été conçu à l’occasion de l’exposition universelle de 1900 et prend place à proximité immédiate des Champs-Élysées. Offrant une place de choix à l’acier et au verre, ce palais se reconnaît aisément à son immense coupole de verre évoquant une serre gigantesque. Ce site se décompose en 3 espaces : les Galeries nationales, la Nef et le palais de la Découverte. Que peut-on découvrir au sein de ces imposants volumes ? La Nef, présentant une longueur impressionnante de 240 mètres, accueille divers événementiels de rayonnement international. Le palais de la Découverte, quant à lui, est un musée consacré aux sciences, permettant aux enfants de découvrir des expositions éducatives et d’expérimenter. Enfin, les Galeries du Grand Palais, en tant que telles, accueillent des expositions consacrées à des artistes majeurs (Gauguin, Picasso, Rodin, Greco, Mucha, Man Ray…). [Grand Palais](https://www.grandpalais.fr/fr)

**Recommandations et conseils :** Pour savourer au mieux ces lieux d’exception parisiens, nous vous recommandons de programmer vos visites sur les horaires de basse affluence. Les sites internet de ces structures communiquent fréquemment sur les plages horaires quotidiennes à privilégier. De même, pour une ville touristique de l’importance de Paris, privilégiez dans la mesure du possible un séjour hors saison. Vous bénéficierez ainsi non seulement de tarifs plus attractifs, mais aussi de conditions optimales. Quant à votre mode de transport, nous vous conseillons d’emprunter les transports en commun ou le vélo sur Paris. Vous profiterez ainsi de déplacements plus fluides, moins onéreux et participerez à améliorer la qualité de l’air de la capitale. Excellent séjour parisien !

**Pour aller plus loin :** - [Office de tourisme Paris](https://parisjetaime.com/)
